35980-from-the-easy-chair-volume-2.title: Easy Chair
35980-from-the-easy-chair-volume-2.creator: Unknown
35980-from-the-easy-chair-volume-2.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The songs are familiar, but they have an appealing melancholy unknown before. Their dying cadences murmur like a muffled peal heralding the visionary procession that is passing out of the enchanted realm of youth forever. So the voices of Sylvester's Eve chant the requiem of the year that is dead.

arxiv-2107-05754.title: EvoBA: An Evolution Strategy as a Strong Baseline for Black-Box Adversarial Attacks
arxiv-2107-05754.creator: Andrei Ilie, Marius Popescu, Alin Stefanescu
arxiv-2107-05754.description: Abstract Recent work has shown how easily white-box adversarial attacks can be applied to state-of-the-art image classifiers. However, real-life scenarios resemble more the black-box adversarial conditions, lacking transparency and usually imposing natural, hard constraints on the query budget. We propose EvoBA 1 1 1 All the work is open source: https://github.com/andreiilie1/BBAttacks.

arxiv-2108-07676.title: Spectral enclosures for the damped elastic wave equation
arxiv-2108-07676.creator: Biagio Cassano, Lucrezia Cossetti, Luca Fanelli
arxiv-2108-07676.description: Abstract In this paper we investigate spectral properties of the damped elastic wave equation. Deducing a correspondence between the eigenvalue problem of this model and the one of Lamé operators with non self-adjoint perturbations, we provide quantitative bounds on the location of the point spectrum in terms of suitable norms of the damping coefficient.

arxiv-2206-12411.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization
arxiv-2206-12411.creator: Wenhao Gao, Tianfan Fu, Jimeng Sun, Connor W. Coley
arxiv-2206-12411.description: Abstract Molecular optimization is a fundamental goal in the chemical sciences and is of central interest to drug and material design. In recent years, significant progress has been made in solving challenging problems across various aspects of computational molecular optimizations, emphasizing high validity, diversity, and, most recently, synthesizability.

arxiv-2309-09156.title: Consensus-Based Leader-Follower Formation Tracking for Control-Affine Nonlinear Multiagent Systems * Thanks: * This work received support in part from the Office of Naval Research (Grant No. N000141712622) and from a joint award from Microsoft Corporation, 1 Microsoft Way, Redmond, WA 98052, USA and
arxiv-2309-09156.creator: Clinton Enwerem, John S. Baras
arxiv-2309-09156.description: Abstract In the typical multiagent formation tracking problem centered on consensus, the prevailing assumption in the literature is that the agents’ nonlinear models can be approximated by integrator systems, by their feedback-linearized equivalents, or by dynamics composed of deterministic linear and nonlinear terms. The resulting approaches associated with such assumptions, however, are hardly applicable to general nonlinear systems.

arxiv-2403-04464.title: Confronting compositional confusion through the characterisation of the sub-Neptune orbiting HD 77946 2023 Confronting compositional confusion through the characterisation of the sub-Neptune orbiting HD 77946 – 7
arxiv-2403-04464.creator: L. Palethorpe, A. Anna John, A. Mortier, J. Davoult, T. G. Wilson, K. Rice, A. C. Cameron, Y. Alibert, L. A. Buchhave, L. Malavolta, J. Cadman, M. López-Morales, X. Dumusque, A. M. Silva, S. N. Quinn, V. Van Eylen, S. Vissapragada, L. Affer, D. Charbonneau, R. Cosentino, A. Ghedina, R. D. Haywood, D
arxiv-2403-04464.description: Abstract We report on the detailed characterization of the HD 77946 planetary system. HD 77946 is an F5 ( M ∗ M_{*} = 1.17 M ⊙ , R ∗ R_{*} = 1.31 R ⊙ ) star, which hosts a transiting planet recently discovered by NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ), classified as TOI-1778 b.

arxiv-2409-15428.title: Supersymmetric Carroll Galileons in Three Dimensions
arxiv-2409-15428.creator: Utku Zorba, Ilayda Bulunur, Oguzhan Kasikci, Mehmet Ozkan, Yi Pang, Mustafa Salih Zog
arxiv-2409-15428.description: Abstract We present the first example of an interacting Carroll supersymmetric field theory with both temporal and spatial derivatives, belonging to the Galileon class, where the non-linear field equation remains second-order in derivative. To achieve this, we introduce two novel tools.

arxiv-2412-17642.title: Characterization of Double-Arborescences and their Minimum-Word-Representants
arxiv-2412-17642.creator: Tithi Dwary, K. V. Krishna
arxiv-2412-17642.description: Abstract A double-arborescence is a treelike comparability graph with an all-adjacent vertex. In this paper, we first give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization of double-arborescences, where we prove that double-arborescences are precisely P 4 P_{4} -free treelike comparability graphs. Then, we characterize a more general class consisting of P 4 P_{4} -free distance-hereditary graphs using split-decomposition trees.

arxiv-2501-02793.title: Fairness Through Matching
arxiv-2501-02793.creator: Kunwoong Kim kwkim.online@gmail.com, Insung Kong insung.kong@utwente.nl, Jongjin Lee jjlee_.lee@samsung.com, Minwoo Chae mchae@postech.ac.kr, Sangchul Park parks@snu.ac.kr, Yongdai Kim ydkim0903@gmail.com
arxiv-2501-02793.description: Abstract Group fairness requires that different protected groups, characterized by a given sensitive attribute, receive equal outcomes overall. Typically, the level of group fairness is measured by the statistical gap between predictions from different protected groups. In this study, we reveal an implicit property of existing group fairness measures, which provides an insight into how the group-fair models behave.

arxiv-2510-10741.title: Cluster and Halo Structures of Light Nuclei within the NUCLEI-PACK Framework
arxiv-2510-10741.creator: H. M. Maridi
arxiv-2510-10741.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by H. M. Maridi. As part of the ongoing NUCLEI-PACK project, this study presents a semi-classical framework for exploring the microscopic geometry of light and exotic nuclei based on optimized sphere packing of nucleons and clusters. Starting from explicit nucleon coordinates generated by the packing algorithm, the model provides direct access to charge, matter, and core–valence radii, allowing quantitative analysis of clustering and halo formation.

arxiv-2511-00547.title: Efficient Generation of Binary Magic Squares
arxiv-2511-00547.creator: Alain Riou
arxiv-2511-00547.description: Abstract We propose a simple algorithm for generating Binary Magic Squares (BMS), i.e., square binary matrices where the sum of all rows and all columns are equal. We show by induction that our algorithm always returns valid BMS with optimal theoretical complexity.

arxiv-2512-05907.title: From Text to Returns: Using Large Language Models for Mutual Fund Portfolio Optimization and Risk-Adjusted Allocation Journal: Knowledge Based Systems
arxiv-2512-05907.creator: Abrar Hossain, Mufakir Qamar Ansari, Haziq Jeelani, Monia Digra, Fayeq Jeelani Syed
arxiv-2512-05907.description: Abstract Generative AI (GenAI) is transforming diverse sectors, from healthcare to natural language processing, by solving complex, data-intensive problems with unprecedented efficiency. In finance, GenAI offers an immense potential in addressing critical challenges such as portfolio optimization and risk management—key pillars of modern finance that ensure strategic asset allocation and risk mitigation.

arxiv-2602-06854.title: SEMA: Simple yet Effective Learning for Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks
arxiv-2602-06854.creator: Mingqian Feng, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang, Jialin Song, Xuekai Zhu, Chenliang Xu, Jianfeng Gao
arxiv-2602-06854.description: Abstract Multi-turn jailbreaks capture the real threat model for safety-aligned chatbots, where single-turn attacks are merely a special case. Yet existing approaches break under exploration complexity and intent drift. We propose SEMA, a simple yet effective framework that trains a multi-turn attacker without relying on any existing strategies or external data. SEMA comprises two stages.

arxiv-2606-05860.title: GenAutoML: An Agentic Framework for Dynamic Architecture Generation and Optimization in Time-Series Analysis
arxiv-2606-05860.creator: Oleeviya Babu Poikarayil, Cédric Schockaert, Abdulrahman Nahhas, Christian Daase, Mursal Dawodi, Jawid Ahmad Baktash, [0.5ex] Paul Wurth S.A, Luxembourg

lemery-course-of-chymistry-1677.description: The 1677 English translation of Lemery's Cours de Chymie; the bestselling chemistry textbook of the late 17th century.

pmc-10513226.title: Comparative analysis of the complete chloroplast genome of Papaveraceae to identify rearrangements within the Corydalis chloroplast genome
pmc-10513226.creator: Sang-Chul Kim, Young-Ho Ha, Beom Kyun Park, Ju Eun Jang, Eun Su Kang, Young-Soo Kim, Tae-Hee Kimspe, Hyuk-Jin Kim, Tzen-Yuh Chiang, Tzen-Yuh Chiang, Tzen-Yuh Chiang
pmc-10513226.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Chloroplast genomes are valuable for inferring evolutionary relationships. We report the complete chloroplast genomes of 36 Corydalis spp. and one Fumaria species. We compared these genomes with 22 other taxa and investigated the genome structure, gene content, and evolutionary dynamics of the chloroplast genomes of 58 species, explored the structure, size, repeat sequences, and divergent hotspots of these genomes, conducted phylogenetic analysis, and identified nine types of chloroplast genome structures among Corydalis spp.

pmc-10578126.title: In silico protein dynamics in the human cytoplasm: Partial folding, misfolding, fold switching, and non‐native interactions
pmc-10578126.creator: Premila P. Samuel Russell, Meredith M. Rickard, Mayank Boob, Martin Gruebele, Taras V. Pogorelov
pmc-10578126.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). We examine the influence of cellular interactions in all‐atom models of a section of the Homo sapiens cytoplasm on the early folding events of the three‐helix bundle protein B (PB). While genetically engineered PB is known to fold in dilute water box simulations in three microseconds, the three initially unfolded PB copies in our two cytoplasm models using a similar force field did not reach the native state during 30‐microsecond simulations.

pmc-10720121.title: Cardiovascular risk and renal injury profile in subjects with type 2 diabetes and non-albuminuric diabetic kidney disease
pmc-10720121.creator: Maurizio Di Marco, Sabrina Scilletta, Nicoletta Miano, Nicola Marrano, Annalisa Natalicchio, Francesco Giorgino, Stefania Di Mauro, Agnese Filippello, Alessandra Scamporrino, Paola Tribulato, Giosiana Bosco, Francesco Di Giacomo Barbagallo, Roberto Scicali, Agostino Milluzzo, Teresa Ballirò, Lucia F
pmc-10720121.description: BackgroundIn the last years, the classical pattern of diabetic kidney disease (DKD) has been partially overcome, because of the uncovering of a new DKD phenotype with significant renal dysfunction without presence of albuminuria: the non-albuminuric DKD (NA-DKD). To date, the cardiovascular risk associated with this phenotype is still debated.

pmc-11390804.title: Correction: Characterizing Family Contextual Factors and Relationships with Child Behavior and Sleep Across the Buffering Toxic Stress Consortium
pmc-11390804.creator: Tiffany Phu, Elly Miles, Amy Dominguez, Jason Hustedt, Sarah Enos Watamura, BTS Consortium Principal Investigators
pmc-11390804.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). itten by Phu, T., Miles., E., Dominguez, A., Hustedt, J., Watamura, S.E., and BTS Consortium Principal Investigators, was originally published electronically on the publisher’s internet portal on 26 May 2021 without open access.

pmc-11475039.creator: Imrul Mosaddek Ahmed, Umme Aktari Nadira, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Fangbin Cao, Zhong-Hua Chen, Eva Vincze, Feibo Wu
pmc-11475039.description: mistake. At the beginning, we serially numbered all protein spots and screened the protein spots for mass spectrometry analysis. However, when writing MS, in order to facilitate the readers’ comprehension of the results, we re-classified and numbered them according to traits such as tolerances to salt (S), drought (D) and D+S, which caused confusion and misalignment.

pmc-12829770.title: Incomplete penetrance in inborn errors of immunity: A skeleton in the closet—The sequel
pmc-12829770.creator: Dusan Bogunovic
pmc-12829770.description: Incomplete penetrance in genetic disorders can be influenced by genetic variant quality, genetic and epigenetic modification, environment, and mosaicism. Introduction Primary immunodeficiencies (PIDs) or inborn errors of immunity (IEIs) are a heterogeneous group of monogenic lesions, resulting in severe infections, disorders of immune hyperactivation, or cancers.

pmc-13107264.title: Phylogenetic Analyses of True Ladybirds (Coleoptera: Coccinellidae: Coccinellini) Reveal Directionality in Diet Evolution and Support a Boreotropical Origin of the Tribe
pmc-13107264.creator: Romain Nattier, Noémie M.‐C. Hévin, Pascaline Chifflet‐Belle, Jiajia Dong, Hermes E. Escalona, Julien M. Haran, Jean‐Claude Streito, Wioletta Tomaszewska, Adam Slipiński, Andreas Zwick, Gael J. Kergoat
pmc-13107264.description: True ladybirds (Coleoptera: Coccinellidae: Coccinellini) are an iconic and beloved group of insects comprising c. 1000 species. Contrary to common belief, true ladybirds are not restricted to temperate areas in the Northern hemisphere and can be found on every continent (with the exception of Antarctica).

pmc-13151285.title: Analysis of predictive factors for post-orthodontic stability: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13151285.creator: Xiaochen Zhang, Axian Wang, Xu Zhang, Haolin Zhang, Zixuan Chen, Xulin Liu, Bin Yan, Xiaodong Zhang, Zexu Gu, Yanning Ma, Zuolin Jin
pmc-13151285.description: Background​​ Orthodontic relapse remains a challenge in clinical practice. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the independent contributions and time-dependent patterns of multidimensional factors influencing the relapse risk, to provide insights for formulating personalized stability strategies.Methods​​ This multi-center retrospective cohort study included 474 participants with a median follow-up of 6 years. Variables included baseline, anatomical, treatment, and retention factors.

pmc-13485913.title: Navigating bibliometric indicators in university rankings: a conceptual framework for strategic research management
pmc-13485913.creator: Wael Alkattan, Asma Terkawi, Mohamad Bakir, Mohammad Alaa Mufti, Karam Hamweyah
pmc-13485913.description: The increasing prominence of global university rankings has fundamentally transformed the strategic landscape of higher education institutions worldwide. This review examines the strategic application of bibliometric indicators, with particular emphasis on Field-Weighted Citation Impact (FWCI), in the context of university ranking systems.
